headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while Cognee handles personal and finance data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP, so it can ingest content from Cognee outputs if they are placed in shared files or servers. Cognee has agentic user/tenant isolation and CLI-only tool use, which reduces but does not eliminate bridging. The shared-file/MCP pathway is plausible in default setups, so interaction risk is medium.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are written into a workspace file or MCP-fed artifact that Roo Code reads as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared filesystem or MCP server, Roo Code can parse attacker-controlled content from Cognee outputs.
mitigations: Keep Cognee outputs out of shared workspace files.
Disable MCP connections between the agents.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on Cognee-generated text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files, Roo Code can expose sensitive content to external model APIs or MCP servers. That makes leakage plausible in default workflows and potentially irreversible once transmitted.
conditions: IF Cognee stores personal or finance data in files accessible to Roo Code, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server, sensitive Cognee data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store sensitive Cognee data outside Roo Code workspaces.
Restrict Roo Code to a redacted subset of files.
Disable or narrow network egress for Roo Code.
Rotate any exposed secrets immediately after a shared-workspace test.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with shared state via session memory, while Roo Code supports multiple instances with filesystem-shared workspace state and can modify git state. Both can write to overlapping mutable resources if co-located, and neither profile shows locking or coordination. That creates a high likelihood of conflicting writes and repository corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF Cognee persists session state into files that Roo Code also edits, state corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on files, run shells, and modify git state, so if it consumes Cognee outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or commands. Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which Roo Code may treat as actionable guidance. The downstream action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Cognee-generated decisions or workflows without verification, it may execute incorrect actions.
IF Cognee outputs are converted into shell commands, git commits, or browser actions, mistakes can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human approval before Roo Code executes Cognee-derived actions.
Force Roo Code to cite source files before acting.
Use a validation checklist for Cognee outputs.
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode during analysis.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Roo Code can read workspace files and transmit them via configured model APIs or MCP servers. If EU or regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create residency or retention mismatches and unauthorized disclosure. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or finance data is stored in files accessible to Roo Code, compliance exposure arises.
IF Roo Code forwards those files to a third-party model API or MCP server, residency and retention obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code-accessible folders.
Use a local-only model for sensitive tasks.
Review retention settings for all configured APIs.
Document a data-handling policy for shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing and audit logs.
